text: The story of the lighthouse and the cottage is not just a memory; it becomes a lesson in patience. The tide is a constant force, and the tower is a small obstacle in its path. To understand the tide, you must understand the water itself. The tide is not a thing to be measured with precision, but a phenomenon to be observed. When the water pulls back, it reveals the shore, and when it comes in, it covers the same places. The lighthouse stands at the edge of this pull, a fixed point against the moving current. It does not fight the tide; it simply allows it to move over it. This is the essence of the place. The shadow of the tower stretches and contracts with the changing water, and in that movement, one can feel the time. The tide is not just water; it is a reminder of the passage of time. The tower, though silent, holds the memory of the tide. The shadow moves with the tide in a way that seems almost deliberate, as if the water itself has a will. This is the power of the small. The tide does not care about our expectations, and neither should we. To measure the tide, we must accept that the measurement will change with the day. The tide is a teacher
